```

```

The important part of this command being:

```
mesa_libs=/home/tcroc/dev/BlockyBallOT/submodules/godot-nir-static
```

We have a few modifications in our fork that allows us more granular control over the compiler toolchain used.  Here's the PRs for reference:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101046
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101045
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101043
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101042
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100982

and this additional pr on our godot-nir-static fork:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot-nir-static/pull/21

They are all very simple PRs.  I just listed them out for the sake of clarity.  I do not expect they have any impact on this error.  But please correct me if I'm wrong.

The godot-nir-static repo is built from source as a submodule within our project.  The directory structure after building looks like:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d2c13d9-db90-4802-98dc-80a983b35361)

And the command we use to build it is:

```
scons platform=windows arch=x86_64 use_llvm=true platform_tools=false import_env_vars=ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR,ZIG_LOCAL_CACHE_DIR use_mingw=true -j 16 CC=/home/tcroc/dev/BlockyBallOT/submodules/godot-src/gitignore/wrapper-scripts/zig-cc.sh CXX=/home/tcroc/dev/BlockyBallOT/submodules/godot-src/gitignore/wrapper-scripts/zig-c++.sh LINK=/home/tcroc/dev/BlockyBallOT/submodules/godot-src/gitignore/wrapper-scripts/zig-c++.sh AS=/home/tcroc/dev/BlockyBallOT/submodules/godot-src/gitignore/wrapper-scripts/zig-c++.sh AR=/home/tcroc/dev/BlockyBallOT/submodules/godot-src/gitignore/wrapper-scripts/zig-ar.sh RANLIB=/home/tcroc/dev/BlockyBallOT/submodules/godot-src/gitignore/wrapper-scripts/zig-ranlib.sh RC=/home/tcroc/dev/BlockyBallOT/submodules/godot-src/gitignore/wrapper-scripts/zig-rc.sh
```

I tested with a local build of `godot-nir-static` (with the default toolchain configuration, on Linux with mingw-gcc) and I can't reproduce the issue.

The difference is it appears that the one that doesn't work uses ``-isystem`` and the one that works uses ``-I`` when supplying  the includes:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b69338f-500b-4671-8e35-893ed7c52128)

So the issue is probably an include order bug which already existed, but worked by chance before.

`-isystem` differs from `-I` in that those paths will be included *after* regular `-I` include paths. So there might now be another header that takes precedence (or no longer does) and defines something that conflicts with OpenGL's definitions for `GL_APIENTRY`. Most likely culprit is our beloved `windows.h`...

That's paired with the very hacky buildsystem we have for Mesa NIR, which globs everything, from its own admission:
```
# We have to blacklist some because we are bindly adding every Mesa directory
# to the include path and in some cases that causes the wrong header to be included.
```

I can't reproduce the error myself so I'm not sure how to debug further, but the whole setup is very brittle. We can revert that one to `CPPPATH` but it's bound to break again when a cosmic ray looks at our Python logic sideways.
This is significantly more complex than that, it wouldn't help / be possible.
